eyebrow: Lesson 19 · B1 · Good Manners with Family · 20 câu
heading: Borrowing and Sharing
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Good Manners with Family – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 12–15.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Good Manners with Family (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: Always ask before you {borrow|borrow} something from a family member. A simple "May I borrow your book, please?" is all it takes. Taking things without asking is never OK, even at home.

paras.label: B
paras.text: If your sister {lends|lends} you her book, {treat|treat} it well. Don't let the pages get {ripped|ripped}, and don't spill juice on the cover. Give it back in exactly the same {condition|condition} as when she gave it to you. Then she will be happy to lend you other things in the future.

paras.label: C
paras.text: When you return it, thank her: "Thank you! I really enjoyed the book." These words show that you respect her things and {value|value} her kindness.

paras.label: D
paras.text: In a family, everyone shares. You share your home, and you share food at the table. You should share your toys and games too. Let your little sister use your {felt-tip pens|felt-tip pens}, or show your brother how to play your new game.

paras.label: E
paras.text: Sharing makes other people feel great because it shows that you want to include them. And let's be honest: most games are more fun with someone else. Sharing is not about losing something; it is about {gaining|gaining} a {playmate|playmate}.

parts.title: Part 1 · Matching headings
parts.instr: Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Mỗi tiêu đề dùng một lần.
options: Saying thanks when you give it back

items.label: Paragraph A
items.why: Đoạn A: hỏi trước khi mượn.

items.label: Paragraph B
items.why: Đoạn B: giữ gìn đồ mượn, trả nguyên vẹn.

items.label: Paragraph C
items.why: Đoạn C: cảm ơn khi trả.

items.label: Paragraph D
items.why: Đoạn D: chia sẻ nhà, đồ ăn, đồ chơi.

items.label: Paragraph E
items.why: Đoạn E: lý do chia sẻ đáng làm.

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: What should you do before you borrow something?
options: Wait until the owner goes out.

questions.q: The writer says it is fine to take things without asking at home.
questions.why: Sai. *Taking things without asking is never OK, even at home.*

questions.q: According to (B), why should you return things in good condition?
options: so the owner will lend you things again
so you can sell them later
because your parents will check them
so you can keep them longer
questions.why: *Then she will be happy to lend you other things in the future.*

questions.q: How are the verbs **borrow** and **lend** used in the text?
options: You borrow from someone; they lend to you.
They mean exactly the same thing.
You lend from someone; they borrow to you.
Borrow is for books; lend is for toys.
questions.why: *borrow something from a family member* / *your sister lends you her book.*

questions.q: According to (E), most games are more fun when you play alone.
questions.why: Sai. *most games are more fun with someone else.*

questions.q: *Sharing is not about losing something; it is about gaining a playmate.* What does this mean?
options: When you share, you get company in return.
You will lose your toys if you share.
You should only share with friends.
Sharing is a kind of game.
questions.why: Chia sẻ không mất gì mà còn có thêm bạn chơi.

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: What is happening in this picture?
options: A book is being handed over and someone is saying thanks.
Two children are arguing over a book.
A boy is tearing a book.
A girl is reading a diary.
questions.alt: A boy hands a book to a girl; a speech bubble says: Thank you!

questions.q: If the boy is giving back a book he borrowed, what should it look like?
options: the same as when he borrowed it
questions.why: *in exactly the same condition as when she gave it to you.*
questions.alt: A boy hands a book to a girl; a speech bubble says: Thank you!

questions.q: Which advice from the text are the children following?
questions.why: Đoạn D: *Let your little sister use your felt-tip pens.*
questions.alt: A girl and a boy sit at a table drawing together with felt-tip pens

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: For my birthday, I got a new video game. [1] At first, I didn't want to let him touch it. [2] Now we play it together every weekend. [3]
options: My little brother kept asking if he could have a go.
I sold it the next day because it was so boring.
My brother broke it as soon as he touched it.
But then Mum reminded me that games are more fun with two players, so I showed him how to play.
He's actually better at it than I am!

items.why: Chuyển biến: từ không muốn → chia sẻ.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *Don't let the pages get ripped* (B). **Ripped** means…
*…in exactly the same condition* (B). **Condition** here means…
*…it is about gaining a playmate* (E). A **playmate** is…
